title.value: Exome sequencing identifies rare damaging variants in ATP8B4 and ABCA1 as risk factors for Alzheimer’s disease
title.quote: # Exome sequencing identifies rare damaging variants in ATP8B4 and ABCA1 as risk factors for Alzheimer’s disease

design.value: Multistage exome-wide gene-based rare-variant burden analysis (stage 1 discovery, independent stage 2 confirmation, fixed-effect meta-analysis, plus a merged mega-sample and a GWAS-locus-targeted burden analysis)
design.quote: Multistage gene burden analysis in exome sequencing data from 32,558 individuals identifies rare damaging variants in ATP8B4 and ABCA1 as risk factors for Alzheimer’s disease.

n.quote: Here, we compared the gene-based burden of rare damaging variants in exome sequencing data from 32,558 individuals—16,036 AD cases and 16,522 controls.

n_description.value: Individuals with exome sequencing data compared in the combined stage 1 + stage 2 meta-analysis: 16,036 AD cases and 16,522 controls (stage 1 was 12,652 cases and 8,693 controls, n = 21,345; stage 2 was 3,384 cases and 7,829 controls, n = 11,213)
n_description.quote: Here, we compared the gene-based burden of rare damaging variants in exome sequencing data from 32,558 individuals—16,036 AD cases and 16,522 controls.

population.value: Individuals of European ancestry only (non-European ancestry samples removed at QC), comprising AD cases diagnosed by NIA-AA or NINCDS-ADRDA criteria — 4,060 early-onset (age at onset ≤65 years) and 8,592 late-onset (age at onset >65 years) cases in stage 1 — and controls not diagnosed with AD; carriers of pathogenic PSEN1, PSEN2, APP or other Mendelian dementia variants and relatives up to the third degree were removed
population.quote: samples were removed when they had high missingness, high contamination, a discordant genetic sex annotation, non-European ancestry, high numbers of new variants
population.location: Methods, Sample processing, genotype calling and QC

comparator.value: Controls not diagnosed with AD (8,693 in stage 1 and 7,829 in stage 2; 16,522 in total), sequenced on the same paired-end Illumina platforms as cases
comparator.quote: otherwise, samples were classified as late-onset AD (366 samples). Controls were not diagnosed with AD. All contributing datasets were sequenced using a paired-end Illumina platform
comparator.location: Methods, Sample processing, genotype calling and QC

biomarker_confirmation.value: AD was diagnosed clinically (NIA-AA or NINCDS-ADRDA criteria); where possible, supportive evidence of an AD pathophysiological process such as cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers was sought, or the diagnosis was confirmed by neuropathological examination
biomarker_confirmation.quote: When possible, supportive evidence for an AD pathophysiological process was sought (including cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers) or the diagnosis was confirmed by neuropathological examination
biomarker_confirmation.location: Methods, Sample processing, genotype calling and QC

outcomes.name: Exome-wide significant association of rare predicted damaging variants in ATP8B4 and ABCA1 with AD risk (new genes)
outcomes.effect_estimate: ATP8B4 (LOF + REVEL ≥ 25) meta-analysis OR 1.5; ABCA1 (LOF + REVEL ≥ 75) meta-analysis OR 1.7
outcomes.quote: we observed a significant association of rare, predicted damaging variants in ATP8B4 and ABCA1 with AD risk, and a suggestive signal in ADAM10

outcomes.name: ATP8B4 rare-variant burden (LOF + REVEL ≥ 25), stage 1, stage 2 and meta-analysis
outcomes.effect_estimate: OR 1.5 in the meta-analysis (stage 1 OR 1.5; stage 2 OR 1.4)

outcomes.name: ABCA1 rare-variant burden (LOF + REVEL ≥ 75), stage 1, stage 2 and meta-analysis
outcomes.effect_estimate: OR 1.7 in the meta-analysis (stage 1 OR 1.7; stage 2 OR 1.6)

outcomes.name: Genes whose rare damaging variant burden was confirmed as associated with AD in the stage 1 + stage 2 meta-analysis
outcomes.effect_estimate: 5 genes: SORL1, TREM2, ABCA7, ATP8B4 and ABCA1
outcomes.quote: This confirmed the AD association of rare damaging variants in the SORL1 , TREM2 , ABCA7 , ATP8B4 and ABCA1 genes.

outcomes.name: Stage 1 discovery: burden tests showing a differential rare-variant burden between AD cases and controls
outcomes.effect_estimate: 13 of 31,204 tests, covering 6 genes (SORL1, TREM2, ABCA7, ATP8B4, ADAM10 and ABCA1)
outcomes.quote: Of all the burden tests performed, 13 tests, covering 6 genes, indicated a differential rare-variant burden between AD cases and controls (false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.1)

outcomes.name: Stage 2 independent confirmation of the stage 1 genes
outcomes.effect_estimate: All stage 1 genes reached P < 0.05 in stage 2; stage 2 effect sizes correlated with stage 1 (Pearson's r on log odds = 0.91)
outcomes.quote: All genes selected in stage 1 reached P < 0.05 (Table , stage 2). The stage 2 effect sizes of these genes correlated with those observed in stage 1 (Pearson’s r on log odds = 0.91).

outcomes.name: ADAM10 rare-variant burden association with AD
outcomes.effect_estimate: Suggestive only; not significant exome-wide after multiple-testing correction
outcomes.quote: The association signal of the ADAM10 gene was not significant exome-wide, presumably because prioritized variants in this gene are extremely few and rare

outcomes.name: Exome-wide significance criterion for the meta-analysis
outcomes.p_value: Holm–Bonferroni corrected P < 0.05 (stage 1 selection at Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.1 across 31,204 tests)
outcomes.quote: For the meta-analysis, genes were considered significantly associated with AD when the corrected P was <0.05 after family-wise correction using the Holm–Bonferroni procedure

outcomes.name: GWAS-locus-targeted burden analysis: candidate driver genes in known AD GWAS loci
outcomes.effect_estimate: Suggestive signals of increased AD risk in RIN3, CLU, ZCWPW1 and ACE among 67 testable genes (187 tests) from the 75 loci of the most recent GWAS
outcomes.quote: our analysis indicated a suggestive signal of increased AD risk in RIN3 , CLU , ZCWPW1 and ACE (FDR < 0.05) (Table and Supplementary Table ); these signals will have to be confirmed in a larger dataset

outcomes.name: Relationship between rare damaging variant burden and age at onset
outcomes.effect_estimate: Increased carrier frequencies in younger cases and larger effect sizes with earlier age at onset
outcomes.quote: For damaging variants in most genes, we observed increased carrier frequencies in younger cases and larger effect sizes were associated with an earlier age at onset ( P = 0.0001)

outcomes.name: Enrichment of the strongest-effect variants in early-onset AD
outcomes.effect_estimate: Loss-of-function variants with the strongest effects are enriched in early-onset AD cases
outcomes.quote: Variants associated with the strongest effect on AD risk, in particular loss-of-function variants, are enriched in early-onset AD cases.

outcomes.name: Carrier frequency of predicted damaging variants across the ten identified genes
outcomes.effect_estimate: Up to 18% of EOAD and 14% of LOAD cases versus 9% of controls
outcomes.quote: Up to 18% EOAD and 14% LOAD cases carried at least 1 predicted damaging variant in 1 of the 10 genes, compared to 9% of the controls

outcomes.name: Attributable fraction of cases explained by rare variants in a specific gene
outcomes.effect_estimate: 0.1% to 2.4% of EOAD cases per gene; 0 to 1.3% of LOAD cases
outcomes.quote: The fractions of EOAD cases in our sample that could be attributed to a rare variant in a specific gene ranged between 0.1 and 2.4%

outcomes.name: Interaction between the rare-variant AD association and APOE-ε4 dosage
outcomes.quote: in a separate analysis we observed no interaction effects between the rare-variant AD association and APOE-ε4 dosage

outcomes.name: Age-matched sensitivity analysis of the ten identified genes
outcomes.effect_estimate: Supported a role in AD for all ten identified genes
outcomes.quote: We performed an age-matched sensitivity analysis to investigate possible effects from other age-related conditions, which supported a role in AD for all ten identified genes

primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The discovery analysis succeeded on its own terms: ATP8B4 and ABCA1 reached exome-wide significance as new AD risk genes in the stage 1 + stage 2 meta-analysis, alongside confirmation of SORL1, TREM2 and ABCA7, while ADAM10 remained only suggestive.
primary_endpoint_status.quote: Together, we report ATP8B4 and ABCA1 as new AD risk factors with exome-wide significance and we report suggestive evidence for the association of rare variants in the ADAM10 gene with AD risk.

multiplicity.approach: Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.1 across the 31,204 stage 1 burden tests to select genes for confirmation; one-sided stage 2 testing in the direction observed in stage 1; family-wise Holm–Bonferroni correction (P < 0.05) across all 31,204 tests for the fixed-effect meta-analysis; a stricter Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05 for the GWAS-targeted analysis because it had no separate confirmation stage
multiplicity.quote: For the meta-analysis, genes were considered significantly associated with AD when the corrected P was <0.05 after family-wise correction using the Holm–Bonferroni procedure

conflicts: The authors declare no competing interests.
limitations: The study was powered only for large effects or common carrier frequencies: 'this analysis has only the power to discover genes for which either the differential variant burden is associated with a large effect size, and/or genes for which large numbers of damaging variant carriers are observed'.
Estimated power to reach P < 1 × 10 −6 in stage 1 was only 41, 22, 11 and 4% across the four deleteriousness thresholds.
The ADAM10 signal could not be confirmed exome-wide: 'the signal can be confirmed only in larger datasets'.

The GWAS driver-gene signals in RIN3, CLU, ZCWPW1 and ACE are suggestive: 'these signals will have to be confirmed in a larger dataset' and 'Larger datasets will be required to further confirm these signals.'
Site-specific technical bias: 'We observed site-specific technical biases, since data were generated at multiple centers, using heterogeneous methods'.
Samples were restricted to European ancestry — samples with 'non-European ancestry' were removed at QC.
'Since APOE status was used as the selection criterion in several contributing datasets, burden tests were not adjusted for APOE-ε4 dosage'.
'damaging variants (including APOE-ε4 / ε4 ) were observed in only 30% of the EOAD cases (Supplementary Table ), suggesting that additional damaging variants are yet to be discovered'.
'the effect of structural variants such as copy number variants and repetitive sequences will need to be investigated in future analyses'.
Genes with a cumulative minor allele count below 10 could not be analysed at all, and only 13,222 of 19,822 autosomal protein-coding genes were tested at the most permissive threshold.

risk_of_bias.domain: Batch / centre effects in sequencing data
risk_of_bias.judgement: Data were generated at multiple centres with heterogeneous methods, producing site-specific technical biases that required dedicated quality-control procedures.
risk_of_bias.quote: We observed site-specific technical biases, since data were generated at multiple centers, using heterogeneous methods

risk_of_bias.judgement: APOE status was a selection criterion in several contributing datasets, so burden tests could not be adjusted for APOE-ε4 dosage; the interaction analysis had to be run on a reduced dataset.
risk_of_bias.quote: Since APOE status was used as the selection criterion in several contributing datasets, burden tests were not adjusted for APOE-ε4 dosage

risk_of_bias.domain: Age differences between cases and controls
risk_of_bias.judgement: The document recognised that age-related conditions could explain the effects and addressed this with an age-matched, propensity-weighted sensitivity analysis that supported all ten genes.
risk_of_bias.quote: We determined if the observed effects could be explained by age differences between cases and controls.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Only European-ancestry samples were retained, so the gene burdens are not established in other ancestries.
risk_of_bias.quote: samples were removed when they had high missingness, high contamination, a discordant genetic sex annotation, non-European ancestry

risk_of_bias.domain: Partial data for a subset of samples (exome extracts)
risk_of_bias.judgement: Some contributing samples were exome extracts containing only reads covering the ten stage 1 genes, and these were excluded from the mega-sample GWAS burden analysis.
risk_of_bias.quote: Exome extract samples only contained the raw reads that cover the ten genes identified in stage 1.

disagreements.question: Do rare variants in ADAM10 associate with AD risk?
disagreements.position: This document reports that two rare ADAM10 missense variants previously reported to segregate incompletely with late-onset AD did not associate with AD in its own data, and that its own ADAM10 signal remained suggestive rather than exome-wide significant.
disagreements.quote: two rare missense variants in ADAM10 were reported before to incompletely segregate with LOAD in a few families (these variants did not associate with AD in our study; Supplementary )

disagreements.question: Can rare-variant burden analysis identify the causal driver genes behind common-variant GWAS loci?
disagreements.position: This document argues that its analysis of rare protein-modifying variants identifies RIN3, CLU, ZCWPW1 and ACE as potential drivers in GWAS loci and thereby addresses a drawback of GWAS.
disagreements.quote: we identified RIN3 , CLU , ZCWPW1 and ACE as potential drivers in GWAS loci, illustrating how analyses of rare protein-modifying variants can solve this drawback of GWAS studies

disagreements.question: Are the ATP8B4 rare-variant associations driven by loss of function?
disagreements.position: This document notes that the odds ratio point estimate for ATP8B4 loss-of-function variants was close to 1, allowing that the driving missense variants may not act through a loss-of-function mechanism.
disagreements.quote: the OR point estimate for ATP8B4 LOF variants was close to 1, allowing for the possibility that the missense variants that drive the ATP8B4 association do not depend on a LOF effect

disagreements.question: Is the rare-variant burden in GWAS loci independent of the GWAS sentinel variant?
disagreements.position: This document concludes that the associations persisted when restricted to very rare variants (MAF < 0.1%), suggesting the rare-variant burden is independent of the GWAS sentinel variant.
disagreements.quote: the AD associations in these genes persisted when focusing on the burden of only the very rare variants (MAF < 0.1%), suggesting that the rare-variant burden is not in linkage with, and thus independent from, the GWAS sentinel variant
